canonical.name: An augmented chain complex over an object is a nonnegative chain complex equipped with an augmentation annihilating the first differential
A coaugmented cochain complex under an object is the dual data of a map from the object into degree zero of a cochain complex
Deleted resolutions are the complexes left after removing the resolved object and its augmentation or coaugmentation
Syzygies and cosyzygies are defined relative to one displayed resolution, not as canonical objects of the category
A projective surjection onto the current kernel extends a partial projective resolution by one exact degree
An injective embedding of the current cokernel extends a partial injective resolution by one exact degree
The iterated free-module construction stays canonical in ZF even when the step from free to projective spends choice
A map of projective resolutions is required to commute with the augmentations over the underlying object map
Projectivity of the degree-zero term lifts a map of resolved objects to degree zero of chosen projective resolutions
If two comparison maps lift the same object map, the next projective term extends a partial homotopy correcting their difference
A projective or injective resolution has a unique homotopy-equivalence class but no preferred comparison map
Two injective resolutions of the same object are homotopy equivalent under that object, though no literal comparison map is canonical
Comparison maps of composites agree only up to homotopy
The chosen comparison of the identity is homotopic to the literal identity map
The degree-zero horseshoe step combines the outer degree-zero projectives into a projective surjection onto the middle object
The first horseshoe kernel fits into a short exact sequence between the outer first syzygies
Repeating the degree-zero lift and kernel exact-sequence step yields the inductive horseshoe construction
Passing the projective horseshoe argument to the opposite abelian category gives the injective horseshoe lemma
Horseshoe resolutions are compatible with morphisms of short exact sequences only up to homotopy
A split short exact sequence yields the evident direct-sum resolution
Two displayed first syzygies need only be stably isomorphic, not canonically equal
The dual Schanuel statement is obtained by passing to the opposite abelian category
A projective object itself is already a length-zero projective resolution
Grothendieck's functorial injective-embedding theorem gives enough injectives and hence injective resolutions for every object
A comparison map between fixed resolutions is unique only up to chain homotopy, not as a literal chain map
The horseshoe middle resolution depends on the chosen lifts and splittings
Grothendieck's theorem is one-sided toward injectives and does not produce enough projectives
The periodic complex ... -> Z/4 -> Z/4 -> Z/4 -> ... with differential 2 is acyclic and degreewise projective but not contractible
